summary: Create automation: convert Confluence 'Flag for review' to Jira ticket and post Slack thread reference
description: Request: build an internal automation that watches Confluence pages for the 'Flag for review' macro (or a page label 'flag-for-review') and automatically creates a scoped Jira issue under the Docs-Review project. The created Jira ticket should include: link to the Confluence page, page excerpt (first 500 chars), page author, and the label/tag that triggered it. Additionally, the automation should post a concise link and ticket reference back into the Slack thread where the flag originated (if flagged via Slack command) or into the #doc-review channel with an excerpt and @mentions of the doc owner. Motivation: current handoff is manual and inconsistent, causing review delays and missing audit trail for regulatory pages. Goal: reduce manual triage time and ensure every flagged doc has a corresponding Jira ticket for tracking and SLA reporting.
impact: Improves doc-review throughput and auditability; reduces missed reviews for compliance docs. Estimated to save ~2-4 manual triage hours per week for Docs and Platform teams.
steps_to_reproduce: Create or identify a Confluence page and add the 'flag-for-review' label OR use the 'Flag for review' macro.
Manually create a Jira ticket (current process) and post link to #doc-review or Slack thread.
Observe that some flagged pages are not tracked and that follow-up is inconsistent.
Desired automation should replicate the manual ticket creation and Slack notification reliably.

acceptance_criteria: When a page is labeled 'flag-for-review' in Confluence, a new Jira issue is created in Docs-Review with link, excerpt, author, and triggering label.
If the flag originates from a Slack thread (via slash command), the bot posts the Jira link back into the thread and mentions the doc author.
Automation deduplicates multiple flags for the same page within a 7-day window and appends comments to the existing ticket instead of creating new ones.
All operations are performed by a service account with minimal required permissions and token rotation policy documented.
Design doc and security checklist completed and approved by Security and Docs leads before rollout.
